question:
An engineer wants to create a backup of Cisco UCS Manager for disaster recovery purposes.
What are two characteristics of a full state backup of a Cisco UCS Manager database? (Choose two.)
options: contains all of the runtime states and statuses but not the configurations
performs a complete binary dump of the database as a .bin file
performs a complete binary dump of the database as a .sql file
performs a complete binary dump of the database as a .tgz file
theory: A Full State backup performs a complete binary dump of the Cisco UCS Manager database, saved with a .bin extension, and captures both the configuration and the runtime state of the system — this is what makes it usable to fully restore or rebuild a fabric interconnect during disaster recovery. In contrast, the XML-based All Configuration/System Configuration/Logical Configuration backups only capture configuration objects (not runtime state) and cannot be used for a system restore, only for configuration import. Recognizing the .bin format and 'includes runtime state + config' are the two defining characteristics of a full state backup. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Configuration Management, Backup Types)
